risk.risk_capacity_notes: Stated tolerance -30% (~57k SEK at current size). REVISED 2026-07-07: the goal is softer than previously recorded (see horizon) — not a hard deadline. That eases the original glidepath tension (a -30% drawdown in year 6 is less catastrophic if the purchase can slip), but vagueness cuts both ways: an uncommitted goal can also crystallize EARLIER or the money be wanted for something else. Treat the glidepath re-anchor trigger (goal becomes concrete) as the operative control, not the calendar.

horizon.primary_goal: Property purchase, nature UNCERTAIN (user statement 2026-07-07): 'not completely sure what I am saving for' — most likely an apartment or similar. One live idea: a Mediterranean vacation apartment, rented out when not used, while renting in Sweden (rental income offsetting Swedish rent). Explicitly vague, not set in stone, a potential long-term goal.
horizon.years_until_needed: 3-7 (SOFT — goal not committed; treat as flexible, not a hard deadline)
horizon.currency_note: If the Mediterranean option materializes, the future liability is EUR, not SEK — this reverses the standing rationale for tilting the equity sleeve toward SEK/Nordic. Flag for the Council whenever the goal firms up.

buffer.notes: Standard buffer confirmed 2026-07-04 — the portfolio's risk budget is genuine, not partly an emergency fund.

cash_flow.recurring_foreign_currency_inflow: ~750-1000 EUR roughly every 2 months, irregular occasions, landing in PayPal (disclosed 2026-07-12). Not salary - described as money that 'comes in at different occasions'.
cash_flow.fx_note: PRIORITY: repeated small FX conversions through PayPal's native conversion are a structural fee-drag risk (PayPal's spread is typically well above mid-market - CONFIRM actual rate, do not assume) that compounds every ~2 months indefinitely. This is a lever #2-class problem (fee drag) even though the sums are small, because it recurs forever. See portfolio.json open_structural_questions 6 for the routing options to evaluate. Do not let 'the amounts are small' excuse ignoring this - it's the recurring nature, not the size of one instance, that makes it structural.

reference_targets.note: v1-amended, ADOPTED by Council ruling 2026-07-07 (same-day amendment to reports/2026-07-07-council-memo.md) - transcribed here 2026-07-12 after discovering it was decided but never written back to this file, a process gap in its own right. Anchor: today treated as T-5 (midpoint of the 3-7y SOFT range in `horizon`); re-anchor trigger is the goal firming up, not the calendar. Equity reverted to 50% (from an initially proposed 45%) because the goal lost its hard deadline: with `horizon.years_until_needed` now soft, the recoverability constraint that justified 45% no longer binds, and 50% sits at the stated -30% drawdown tolerance with zero slack - not beyond it. The 20% SEK/Nordic currency tilt originally proposed alongside 45% was DROPPED (liability currency now unknown - could be SEK or EUR per `horizon.currency_note` - so currency matching is void in both directions; plain global unhedged equity is the neutral stance). SUPERSEDED 2026-07-27 - see ADOPTED_2026-07-27 below; this note and the glidepath_table are retained for history and for the re-anchor trigger, not as the current operating target.
reference_targets.ADOPTED_2026-07-27: User approved the Council's proposed target allocation from reports/2026-07-27-council-memo.md: 85% equity / 5% cash-ballast / ~0% traditional fixed income / 10% crypto. CAVEAT carried forward from the memo, unresolved: no backtest yet confirms 85/10 equity/crypto respects the -30% max drawdown tolerance; the glidepath_table's de-risking schedule should re-engage if/when horizon.primary_goal firms up with a date inside ~3 years.

risk_tier_framework_proposed.status: REVISED 2026-07-22 to 60/30/10 (from 70/20/10) at user's direction. Nested with, not competing against, the exposure-class glidepath: the glidepath still describes composition inside the tiers, but the user has now overridden its fixed-income weight - see fixed_income_stance below. Rationale (user's words 2026-07-22): 'I am ready to take a little risk, but to keep it diversified and mature. I do not have enough money or salary to make a lot of money only from fixed income yet. And I will earn more later on so I have the possibility to have a little bit more risky portfolio.' The larger medium tier (30% vs 20%) reflects appetite for more individual-stock exposure alongside the secure index core. History: 70/20/10 was ADOPTED 2026-07-20, itself carried forward from the original 2026-07-12 proposal.
risk_tier_framework_proposed.fixed_income_stance: USER DIRECTION 2026-07-22: fixed income / savings-account allocation should be VERY SMALL (near-zero). User explicitly accepts total portfolio equity pushing above 70% ('The push of equity above 70% is fine. I don't mind.'). This overrides reference_targets.glidepath_table's now_T5plus 40% fixed_income weight. Reason: at current portfolio size (~200-230k SEK) and income level, fixed income cannot build meaningful wealth; user prefers a diversified, 'mature' equity-led portfolio and expects rising income to support higher risk over time. The glidepath's FI ballast re-engages only if/when the property goal firms up (the re-anchor trigger in reference_targets.note), not now. Any de-risking ballast used before then should favour a short-duration/money-market sleeve over traditional bonds, and kept minimal.

tier_definitions.secure: The majority tier. Still INVESTED (not cash sitting idle) but in low-risk, growing vehicles - diversified/index-style funds. Grows primarily from monthly contributions; not meant to be traded. User's own words: 'I do not want my money to just sit on a bank account or similar and barely move (except from my monthly injections).' Candidate holdings: the undeployed avanza-isk cash (145,559.26 SEK as of 2026-07-20) once allocated to broad index equity/FI, and Avanza Auto 3 pending confirmation of its actual risk profile (open question 8, factsheet still needed).
tier_definitions.medium: Individual stocks with a demonstrated good trend and fundamentals - not passive index holdings. 'Considerately placed and moved once in a while if it is detected it can be better off elsewhere without increasing the risk' (user's words) - i.e. occasional rebalancing within this tier is expected, but each move should hold risk level roughly constant, not ratchet it up. Candidate holdings: SHB-A.ST, INVE-A.ST. Tundra Sustainable Frontier's classification is NOT yet confirmed - frontier-market funds typically carry more risk than 'normal stocks with good trend,' flagged for user confirmation rather than assumed. PROCESS DEFINED 2026-07-28: the vetting/rotation process for this tier is now the `swedish-equity-review` skill (.claude/skills/swedish-equity-review/SKILL.md) - a 6-dimension weighted scoring rubric (business quality, financial strength, valuation, insider activity, dividend quality, growth), invoked on demand rather than every weekly sweep. This is the concrete answer to open_structural_question #16 (medium-tier migration), replacing the previously vague 'one vetted position at a time.'
tier_definitions.high_risk_active: Money the user explicitly states they can afford to lose to a greater extent, managed actively (weekly-ish). Matches CLAUDE.md's existing short-horizon tactical rule (Short <6mo: capped at 10% of portfolio, never High confidence, always flagged tactical) - not a new risk category for this system, the first sweep with real content in it. Candidate holdings: ETH (self-custody) and COIN-XBT.ST (BTC certificate).

risk_tier_framework_proposed.profit_recycling_rule: User-stated operating principle, recorded verbatim in substance: gains realized from the medium and high-risk tiers should flow to the greatest extent into the secure tier, not compound within the riskier tiers. User's framing: 'the money I make from this should to the greatest extent go into the more safer tiers... considered as a monetising machine sort of.' This is a standing instruction for future rebalancing/trim decisions (e.g. the pending COIN-XBT.ST trim, open question 7) - proceeds from trims or sales in medium/high-risk should default toward the secure tier unless the user says otherwise for a specific trade. Not yet implemented in any executed trade; applies going forward.
